# A strict six-ray scalar obstruction and a collapsing proper-cut triangle

This note certifies the failure of a specified necessary-condition
screen. It does not produce compatible critical three-fiber data.
In particular it keeps the common mixed cap budgets and the existence
of a compatible B separate from mere section/chord inequalities.

## 1. A strict scalar certificate with Lambda=1 and determinant one

Start with the actual ordinary triangle

    K_0=conv{(-1,-1),(2,-1),(-1,2)}=-T,
    v_1=(1,0), v_2=(0,1), v_3=(-1,-1).

Its area is k_0=9/2. The sections through 0 all have normalized
length k_i=2, centers zero, and both ray lengths one. Each actual
cap v_i.x>=0 has area q_i=2, and its sorted profile
F_K=q_min+q_mid+q_max/4 is exactly k_0.

Assign the positive A-section data

    a_1=1, a_2=a_3=1/100, a_0=1/100.

Here a_0 denotes the ASSIGNED A area; no A is claimed in this
section. All a_i<k_i, and all centered moment inequalities
|c_i|<=a_i(k_i-a_i)/(k_i+2a_i) are strict at c_i=0.
The section coefficients have

    Lambda_0=1/4+100/101=501/404=:r.

Scale all rays and section lengths by r, and all areas by r^2.
This preserves the canonical normals, so their determinant is one,
and now Lambda=1. The resulting parameters are exactly

    p=(101,200,200)/501,
    t_1=1/4, t_2=t_3=1/202,
    k_i=2r, a_1=r, a_2=a_3=r/100,
    k=(9/2)r^2, a=r^2/100, q_i=2r^2.

They have min p=101/501<2/9, because 909<1002.
All the following proposed screen conditions hold:

* The actual six-ray radial feasibility inequalities hold strictly;
  each compares r with r/2.
* The six-ray core area is L=3r^2<k. Its three double-sector
  triangles have total D_core=3r^2/2.
* With c=128/279, the actual q_i/k=4/9<c and F_K=k.
* The resulting lower area k>=4D_core/(3c) is strict:
  4D_core/(3c)=(279/64)r^2<(9/2)r^2.
* Every full two-line unique-sector envelope has E_i=r^2;
  its mandatory opposite pair triangle has area r^2/2. Therefore
  (1-2c)k=(23/62)r^2< E_i-r^2/2.
* The assigned A area strictly exceeds every two-chord lower bound:
  max a_i a_j/2=r^2/200<a=r^2/100.
* The small-A condition is strict: a/k=1/450<1/31.

Thus these actual-K ray, core, profile, centered-moment, and assigned
A-area constraints do NOT force min p>=2/9. This is an exact rational
certificate, not an inference from a numerical optimization. Except
for the genuine equality F_K=k, it stays away from every relevant
boundary of those inequalities.

## 2. Proper triple cuts do not force convergence of their chords

There is a separate, genuine geometric caution about adding A data.
A family may have small area and all three canonical cuts proper,
yet its positive section on x=-1 need not approach the full length
of its limiting vertical segment.

Fix H>3 and L in (0,H). For a sufficiently small w>0 put

    u=Lw/(H-L), R=u+w=Hw/(H-L).

Let A_w be the triangle whose right vertical edge has x=-1+w,
center ordinate (1-w)/2 and length H, and whose left vertex is

    (-1-u,(1+u)/2).

It is invariant under the affine reflection (x,y)->(x,-x-y).
Its cut x=-1 is proper and has length exactly

    H u/(u+w)=L.

Its other two cuts y=-1 and x+y=1 are proper for small w,
because the vertical endpoints lie strictly on both sides of their
levels. The reflection exchanges these cuts. Direct intersection
with the lower sloping edge gives their equal normalized lengths

    sigma_2=sigma_3=w(H+w-3)/(H-L+w).              (1)

The actual area is

    |A_w|=H R/2=H^2 w/[2(H-L)].                   (2)

It tends to zero while sigma_1=L stays fixed. The limiting set is
the vertical segment on x=-1 of length H, not L. The failure of
section convergence is legitimate: the limiting cut is no longer
proper in a full-dimensional limiting A.

For example H=6,L=1,w=1/100 gives u=1/500,

    sigma_1=1, sigma_2=sigma_3=301/50100,
    |A_w|=9/250.

All three cuts are proper although sigma_1=1<3. Therefore a claim
that small area plus the three proper cuts forces sigma_1>=3-o(1)
would be false. Any repair must retain additional cap-mass or
compatibility information.

## 3. Even adding the ordinary A profile does not fix the ray screen

A reflected version also satisfies the ordinary joint profile.
Take w=1/100, H=10, L=1, u=1/900. Let A be the triangle with left
vertical edge

    x=-101/100, y in [-899/200,1101/200]

and right vertex

    (-899/900,899/1800).

Again the reflection (x,y)->(x,-x-y) preserves A, and the three
canonical cuts are proper. The actual section lengths and area are

    sigma_A1=1, sigma_A2=sigma_A3=699/89900=:e,
    a=1/18.

Together with the ACTUAL K_0=-T above, these satisfy the same
centered chord-moment bounds, six-ray bounds, two-chord area bounds,
and small-area ratio a/k=1/81<1/31. Their full section weights are

    p_1=(1+e)/(5+e)<2/9,
    p_2=p_3=2/(5+e).

Indeed p_1<2/9 is equivalent to 7e<1, which is immediate.
Uniformly scaling the rays and section data again gives Lambda=1
if desired, without changing any of these ratios.

This time retain the ACTUAL A cap volumes U_i at v_i.x>=-1.
The small captured triangle at x>=-1 has area

    U_1=1/1800.

The bottom missed cap at y<-1 is a triangle of height 699/200
and normalized horizontal width e, so reflection gives

    U_2=U_3=1/18-488601/35960000
              =13582591/323640000.

Hence U_1<U_2=U_3 and the ordinary sorted profile satisfies

    F_A=U_1+U_2+U_3/4
       =68632155/1294560000
       <a=71920000/1294560000.

Thus one may add real A, its proper three cuts, its actual small
area and section data, and even F_A<=a to this necessary-condition
screen without obtaining min p>=2/9.

The common mixed budgets DO NOT hold in this construction: K_0 has
q_1=q_2=q_3=2, while U_1 differs from U_2,U_3. Nor is any B with
(A+B)/2 contained in K_0 asserted. These omissions are explicit.
The example isolates why actual common cap budgets and the endpoint
enclosure cannot be replaced by the listed section/area constraints.
